You who believe, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace."
When Allah and the angels share one verb, the verse names both parties in coordination, "Allah and His angels". The grammar of shared action is explicit naming, and this verse is its clearest form.

Qur'an 97:1-4, Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v3, p574 إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ (1) وَما أَدْراكَ ما لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ (2) لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ (3) تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيها بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ (4) inna anzalnahu fi laylati al-qadr. wa-ma adraka ma laylatu al-qadr. laylatu al-qadri khayrun min alfi shahr. tanazzalu al-mala'ikatu wa-al-ruhu fiha bi-idhni rabbihim min kulli amr "We sent it down on the Night of Decree. What will make you understand what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months. The angels and the Spirit descend in it by their Lord's permission with every command."

The Night of Decree does both in one sura. The descent of the Quran is We in the first verse. The angels and the Spirit get their own verb in the fourth, "they descend, by their Lord's permission". The carriers are named, the permission is named, and the We stays the We.

Qur'an 50:16, al-Jadwal fi I'rab al-Qur'an, v30, p52 وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ وَنَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ wa-laqad khalaqna al-insana wa-na'lamu ma tuwaswisu bihi nafsuh. wa-nahnu aqrabu ilayhi min habli al-warid "We created the human being, and We know what his soul whispers to him. We are nearer to him than his jugular vein."

And nearness itself is said in both persons. "We are nearer to him than his jugular vein" is the We. "I am near" (Qur'an 2:186) is the I, as the reports below show. One nearness, two registers, and the pair proves the pronouns carry emphasis.

Qur'an 15:9, as printed in al-Burhan fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, v3, p397 إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وإِنَّا لَه لَحافِظُونَ inna nahnu nazzalna al-dhikra wa-inna lahu la-hafizun "We have sent down the Reminder, and We will surely preserve it."

"We, We sent down the Reminder, and We are its guardians." The doubled We of this verse is the charge's favorite target, and it sits in a book that names Jibril as the carrier of the same sending down (Qur'an 2:97), "upon your heart by Allah's permission", and names the Trustworthy Spirit (Qur'an 26:193) beside it. The sending is one. The We is Allah's. The carriers are named elsewhere, which is exactly where the book wants them.

The grammar layer closes. The Quran's own usage forbids reading number into its pronouns. The remaining question is where the We sits doctrinally, and the answer is next to the book's strictest oneness.
4. Where the We Meets the One God

Source: Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan v3 p328; Majma' al-Bayan v9 p267; al-Mizan v18 p381; Tafsir al-Qummi v2 p448 Question: does the We sit near partnership in the Quran's own arrangement Claim: the We appears inside the book's strongest assertions of oneness, and the school reads those passages as tawhid arguments Basis: Qur'an 51:47-51, 112
If the We carried any scent of partnership, the book would keep it away from its oneness passages. It does the opposite.

Qur'an 51:47-51, Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v3, p328 وَالسَّماءَ بَنَيْناها بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ (47) وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْناها فَنِعْمَ الْماهِدُونَ (48) وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنا زَوْجَيْنِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ (49) فَفِرُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (50) وَلا تَجْعَلُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ إِنِّي لَكُمْ مِنْهُ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ (51) wa-al-sama'a banaynaha bi-aydin wa-inna la-musi'un. wa-al-arda farashnaha fa-ni'ma al-mahidun. wa-min kulli shay'in khalaqna zawjayni la'allakum tadhakkarun. fa-firru ila Allahi inni lakum minhu nadhirun mubin. wa-la taj'alu ma'a Allahi ilahan akhara inni lakum minhu nadhirun mubin "We built the heaven with strength, and We are surely expanding it. We spread out the earth, and how excellent are We at preparing it. We created every thing in pairs, so that you may remember. Flee to Allah. I am a clear warner to you from Him. Do not set up another god beside Allah. I am a clear warner to you from Him."

One passage, three persons. We built, We spread, We created pairs, then the passage breaks into "flee to Allah; I am a warner from Him", then "do not set up with Allah another god". The We lives next door to the first person and to the book's ban on partners. The school's commentators read the passage exactly so.

al-Tabrisi, Majma' al-Bayan, v9, p267 المعنى : ( والسماء بنيناها بأيد ) تقديره وبنينا السماء بنيناها بقوة ، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن زيد وقتادة أي : خلقناها ورفعناها ، على حسن نظامها ( وإنا لموسعون ) أي قادرون على خلق ما هو أعظم منها ... ( والأرض فرشناها ) ... ( فنعم الماهدون ) نحن إذ فعلنا ذلك للمنافع ومصالح العباد ، لا لجر نفع ، ولا لدفع ضرر "The meaning of “We built the sky with strength” is, We built the sky with power. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Qatadah said this means that We created it and raised it in a fine order. “We are fully able” means that We can create what is greater than it. “We spread out the earth.” “How excellent are We at preparing it.” We did this for the benefit and welfare of people. We did not do it to gain benefit or prevent harm."

al-Tabrisi, Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v3, p329 ( وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْناها ) أي بسطناها ومهدناها لمنافع العباد وخلقنا من كل شيء صنفين مثل الليل والنهار ، والأرض والسماء ، والشمس والقمر ، والجن والإنس ، والبر والبحر ، وقيل : الزوجين الذكر والأنثى لكي تعلموا أن خالق هذه الأزواج واحد لا يشبهه أحد "We spread out the earth and prepared it for people's needs. We created everything in pairs, such as night and day, earth and sky, sun and moon, jinn and humans, and land and sea. It is also said that the pair means male and female, so that you may know that the Creator of these pairs is One and that nothing resembles Him."
Al-Tabrisi glosses the We-verses with the tawhid they serve, and his gloss on the pairs runs to the section's point. His short recension of the commentary states it as its own exhibit.

al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, v18, p381 ( بيان ) تشير الآيات إلى عدة من آيات الله الدالة على وحدانيته في الربوبية ورجوع أمر التدبير في الأرض والسماء والناس وأرزاقهم إليه ... والاستنتاج الآتي في آخر هذه الآيات في قوله : ( ففروا إلى الله - إلى أن قال - ولا تجعلوا مع الله إلها آخر ) الآية ، يشهد على أن سوق هذه الآيات والدلائل لاثبات وحدانيته تعالى في الربوبية "Explanation. The verses point to several signs of Allah that prove He alone governs all things. He directs the earth, the sky, people, and their provision. The conclusion at the end says, "Flee to Allah," then, "Do not set up another god with Allah." This shows that these verses and proofs establish that Allah alone rules and governs."

Al-Tabataba'i says the same with the school's full weight. The verses are marshaled to establish His oneness in lordship, and their conclusion is the flight to Allah and the ban on another god. The We is the register the book uses to argue oneness.
The sura of pure oneness answers in the He, the register of the Lord being taught, and its occasion of revelation was a question about lineage.

Tafsir al-Qummi, v2, p448 سورة الاخلاص مكية آياتها خمس ط (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قل هو الله أحد) اي هو الله الأحد وكان سبب نزولها ان اليهود جاءت إلى رسول الله ﵌ فقالت : ما نسب ربك ؟ فأنزل الله (قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد) ومعنى قوله : أحد أحدي النعت كما قال رسول الله ﵌ : نور لا ظلام فيه وعلم لا جهل فيه وقوله : الصمد ، اي الذي لا مدخل فيه وقوله : لم يلد ، اي لم يحدث ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد ، قال : لا له كفو ولا شبيه ولا شريك ولا ظهير ولا معين . "Surat al-Ikhlas was revealed in Mecca. It has five verses. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Say, 'He is Allah, the One.' The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah and asked, "What is your Lord's lineage?" Then Allah revealed, "Say, He is Allah, the One, Allah, the Everlasting Refuge. He did not beget, and He was not born. No one is equal to Him." Ahad means that His attributes are unique. The Messenger of Allah said, "He is a light free of darkness and knowledge free of ignorance." Al-Samad means the One with no opening within Him. "He did not beget" means that He did not bring anything into existence. "He was not born, and no one is equal to Him." He has no equal, no likeness, no partner, no supporter, and no helper."

The Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ, what is your Lord's lineage, and the answer was the sura of the One. The third person here is the presentation of Allah for others to learn of Him. And the gloss al-Qummi transmits closes the helpers question with five denials. No equal, no likeness, no partner, no backer, no helper. The sura that says He is the sura that denies every companion the charge hopes to find inside We.

This layer closes the plurality half of the charge. The We is majesty inside a book that banks its oneness beside it. The confusion half remains, the question of who speaks when the book says He, and the school's answer has three parts, a named device, a named relay, and a named occasion.
5. The Person-Shifts Have a Name

Source: Kanz al-Daqa'iq v1 p118; al-Mizan v3 p377; Sharh Usul al-Kafi v1 p122 and v3 p204; al-Insaf v2 p174; Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan v1 p118; Bihar al-Anwar v18 p173 Claim: the shifts of person in the Quran are the named device iltifat, used with stated purposes, and the He-passages are Allah's own speech carried by a named relay Basis: Qur'an 1:1-7, 2:168, 9:2, 2:186, 69:40

The scholarly form of the charge reads person-shifts as the seams of different authors. The shifts sit inside single sentences (Qur'an 6:99) and single passages (Qur'an 51:47-51), where different hands cannot hide, and the same act carries both pronouns (Qur'an 82:7 and 95:4).

The Fatiha performs the shift in its first five verses. Praise of the Lord of the worlds, all third person, then suddenly the address turns to You alone, second person, and the worshipper is standing before the One he was describing.

al-Mashhadi, Kanz al-Daqa'iq, v1, p118 وفي إيراد « إياك » دون « إياه » ، كما هو مقتضى الظاهر ، التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب . ومن النكتة الخاصة ، في الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ، في هذا المقام ، بعد اشتماله على فائدة عامة ، من جهة المتكلم ، وهي التصرف والافتنان في وجود الكلام واظهار القدرة عليها ، ومن جهة المخاطب ، وهي تطرية نشاطه في سماع الكلام ، وايقاظه للإصغاء إليه . أنه لما قيل : « إياك » بدل « إياه » ، فقد نزل الغائب بواسطة أوصافه المذكورة التي أوجب تميزه وانكشافه ، حتى صار كأنه تبدل خفاء غيبته ، بجلاء حضوره ، منزلة المخاطب في التمييز والظهور "The use of iyyaka carries the speech from referring to someone absent into directly addressing Him. This shift has a general benefit. For the speaker, it shows skill and variety in expression. For the hearer, it renews attention and wakes the listener to hear carefully. Here it has a further purpose. The word iyyaka brings the One previously spoken of through His qualities into the position of one directly addressed. Those qualities distinguished Him and made Him known. The hiddenness of His absence became as clear as His presence. He therefore became like one directly addressed in clarity and distinction."

Al-Mashhadi explains the turn. From the Speaker's side it displays command of the speech. From the hearer's side it wakes attention. And the special benefit here is that the One described by His attributes becomes as if the obscurity of His absence exchanged itself for the clarity of presence. The shift moves the reciter from learning about Allah to addressing Him. It is the opposite of confusion. It is the prayer's engine.
The school's modern tafsir catalogs the device across the book.

al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, v3, p377 وأعلم أن في الآيات موارد من الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن خطاب الجمع إلى خطاب المفرد وبالعكس وفيها موارد من وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير كتكرر لفظ الجلالة في عدة مواضع والنكتة في الجميع ظاهرة للمتأمل "Know that these verses include shifts from speaking about Allah to speaking directly to Him. They also shift between addressing many people and addressing one person. In some places, they use an explicit noun where a pronoun would usually appear, such as repeating the name Allah several times. A thoughtful reader can see the purpose of all these expressions."

Al-Tabataba'i notes the shifts in one passage after another, absence to address, plural to singular, pronoun to explicit noun, and says the purposes are clear to the reflecting reader. The hadith commentary of the school does the same work on the Quran and on the Imams' ﵈ own words.

al-Mazandarani, Sharh Usul al-Kafi, v1, p122 (فقال : إذا قيل لهم) الضمير للناس في قوله تعالى : (يا أيها الناس كلوا مما في الأرض حلالاً طيباً ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان) على سبيل الالتفات من الخطاب إلى الغيبة للتنبيه على بعدهم عن رتبة الخطاب بسبب سلوكهم طريق التقليد "In the words, "When it is said to them," the pronoun refers to the people in Allah's words, "People, eat what is lawful and good on the earth. Do not follow Satan's footsteps." The speech shifts from directly addressing them to speaking about them. This alerts us that following imitation has kept them far from the rank of direct address."

al-Mazandarani, Sharh Usul al-Kafi, v3, p204 (الذي لا يدركنا الغالي) الموصول صفة للنمط الأوسط وإفراده باعتبار اللّفظ والأصل أن يقول لا يدركه بالضمير للموصول إلاّ أنّه أتى بضمير المتكلّم من باب الالتفات من الغيبة إلى التكلّم للتصريح بالمقصود كما في قول أمير المؤمنين (﵇) : «أنا الّذي سمّتني أمي حيدرة» "In “the extremist cannot grasp us,” the relative pronoun describes the middle pattern. It is singular because of its wording. The original wording would be “cannot grasp him,” using a pronoun that refers back to the relative pronoun. The verse brings the first-person pronoun, a shift from the third person to the first. It states the intended meaning plainly, as Amir al-Muminin said, “I am the one my mother named Haydara.”"

One grammar for the book and the house. The Quran shifts from addressing "O mankind" to reporting "when it is said to them", to mark their distance from the rank of address. And Imam al-Rida ﵇ speaks of us, we the middle way whom the extremists cannot grasp, where the base grammar would say him, a shift from third person to first for the sake of stating the object openly, like Ali's ﵇ naming himself Ḥaydara, the one his mother so named. The Imams ﵈ use the device the Quran uses, which settles what kind of device it is.
The Sunni rhetorical tradition reaches the same verdict on the same terms.

al-Iskandari, al-Insaf, v2, p174 ثم التفات من التكلم إلى الغيبة بقوله - واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله - وأصله واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي وأنى ، وفي هذا الالتفات بعد الالتفات الأول افتنان في أساليب البلاغة وتفخيم للشأن وتعظيم للأمر ... وكل هذا من حسنات الفصاحة "Then the speech turns from "We" to speaking about Allah by name in, "Know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah..." Its original form was, "Know that you cannot escape Me, and that I..." This shift, after the first shift, shows variety in eloquent expression. It gives the matter greater weight and importance. All of this belongs to the beauties of eloquence."

Al-Insaf, commenting on al-Zamakhshari, analyzes the shift of Qur'an 9:2 from the first person escape clause to the naming of Allah, and calls the turns virtuosity in the methods of eloquence, magnifying the station and the matter. The verse's base form is first person, and the shift to third is the art. That is the He-question answered in advance, centuries before the charge existed.
The Relay Is Named
Who speaks when the book says He. Allah speaks, and the carriers are named. The clearest statement is the gloss on 69:40.

al-Tabrisi's gloss, in Bihar al-Anwar, v18, p173 وقال في قوله تعالى : " إنه لقول رسول كريم " أي إن القرآن قول رسول كريم على ربه وهو جبرئيل (﵇) ، وهو كلام الله أنزله على لسانه ، ثم وصف جبرئيل فقال : " ذي قوة " أي فيما كلف وامر به من العلم والعمل وتبليغ الرسالة ... " أمين " على وحي الله ورسالاته إلى أنبيائه "Regarding Allah's words, "It is truly the word of a noble messenger," he said that the Quran is the word brought by a noble messenger before his Lord, who is Jibril. It is Allah's speech, which He sent down through Jibril. Allah then describes Jibril, "Possessing strength," meaning strength in the knowledge, actions, and delivery of the message entrusted to him. "Trustworthy," meaning trustworthy with Allah's revelation and His messages to His prophets."

The Quran is the word of a noble messenger toward his Lord, Jibril ﵇, and it is Allah's speech sent down upon his tongue. Add the grammar of the qul-verses, where Allah composes the Prophet's ﷺ exact words, say to them that He is Allah, One, and the architecture is complete. Allah speaks, Jibril carries to the Prophet's ﷺ heart, the Prophet recites, and each layer is grammatically visible in the book. Third-person self-presentation plus named relay is the book's standing design.
The Occasion of the I
One shift has a recorded occasion, and it prepares the next section.

from al-Hasan, in Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v1, p118 روي عن الحسن أن سائلا سأل النبي ( ص ) أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه ؟ فنزلت الآية "Hasan reported that a questioner asked the Prophet, "Is our Lord near, so we may speak quietly to Him, or far, so we must call out to Him?" Then the verse came down."

A questioner asked the Prophet ﷺ whether the Lord is near, that they should whisper, or far, that they should call out. The answer came down without the relay marker. No command to say stands before the answer. The Lord Himself, in the first person, told him He is near, and that is the I of the Quran, the register of nearness and answer.
6. Allah Answers in His Own I

Source: 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida ﵇ v1 p269; al-Kafi v2 p515, v2 p489, v1 p296, v1 p474 Claim: the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt ﵈ show the I as Allah's direct answer, layer We, He, and I inside single reports, and read the pronouns as address Basis: Qur'an 2:186, the Fatiha, Qur'an 97

Qur'an 2:186, Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v1, p118 وَإِذا سَأَلَكَ عِبادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذا دَعانِ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ wa-idha sa'alaka 'ibadi 'anni fa-inni qarib. ujibu da'wata al-da'i idha da'an. fa-l-yastajibu li wa-l-yu'minu bi la'allahum yarshudun "When My servants ask you about Me, I am near. I answer the call of the caller when he calls Me. Let them answer Me and believe in Me, so that they may be rightly guided."
The verse promises nearness in the first person and drops the relay command that stands before most answers, so Allah speaks in His own person. The school's hadith uses this I exactly where it lives.

al-Saduq, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida ﵇, v1, p269 حدثنا محمد بن القاسم المفسر الأسترآبادي ﵁ قال : حدثنا يوسف بن محمد بن زياد وعلي بن محمد بن سيار عن أبويهما عن الحسن بن علي عن أبيه علي بن محمد عن أبيه محمد بن علي عن أبيه الرضا علي بن موسى عن أبيه موسى بن جعفر عن أبيه جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه محمد بن علي عن أبيه علي بن الحسين عن أبيه الحسين بن علي عن أبيه أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب ﵈ قال : قال رسول الله : قال الله ﷿ : قسمت فاتحه الكتاب بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سال إذا قال العبد (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم) قال الله جل جلاله : بدأ عبدي باسمي وحق على أن أتمم له أموره وأبارك له في أحواله فإذا قال : (الحمد لله رب العالمين) قال الله ﷿ : حمدني عبدي وعلم أن النعم التي له من عندي وان البلايا التي دفعت عنه فبطولي أشهدكم انى أضيف له إلى نعم الدنيا نعم الآخرة ... فإذا قال : (إياك نعبد) قال الله ﷿ : صدق عبدي إياي يعبد ... فإذا قال : (اهدنا الصراط المستقيم) إلى آخر السورة قال الله ﷿ : هذا لعبدي ولعبدي ما سال "Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, the commentator from Astarabad, reported from Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, from their fathers, from Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Jafar, from his father Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib. The Messenger of Allah said that Allah said, "I divided the Opening of the Book between Me and My servant. Half belongs to Me, and half belongs to My servant. My servant will receive what he asks for."
When the servant says, "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," Allah says, "My servant began with My name. I will complete his affairs and bless his circumstances."

When the servant says, "Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of all worlds," Allah says, "My servant praised Me. He knows that every blessing he has comes from Me, and that I turned away the trials that missed him through My grace. I call you to witness that I will add the blessings of the next life to his blessings in this life."
When the servant says, "You alone we worship," Allah says, "My servant has spoken truly. He worships Me alone."
When the servant says, "Guide us on the straight path," until the end of the chapter, Allah says, "This belongs to My servant. My servant will receive what he asks for.""

This narration, through the chain of the twelve Imams ﵈ from Ali ﵈ from the Prophet ﷺ from Allah, holds all three persons in one report, and it enacts the very turn al-Mashhadi explained, the described Lord becoming the answering One. The servant recites the taught words of praise about Allah. At each verse Allah answers in His own first person, that His servant has praised Him, that it is due upon Him to complete his affairs, that it is Him the servant worships. The recited book carries the description. The answering Lord carries the I. The relay carries the names. One report shows the whole grammar of the three persons, and the school transmits it as the liturgy of every prayer.

Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, al-Kafi, v2, p515 علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن صفوان بن يحيى ، عن إسحاق بن عمار ، عن بعض أصحابه ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : إن لله ﷿ ثلاث ساعات في الليل وثلاث ساعات في النهار يمجد فيهن نفسه ... يقول : إني أنا الله رب العالمين ، إني أنا الله العلي العظيم ، إني أنا الله العزيز الحكيم ، إني أنا الله الغفور الرحيم ، إني أنا الله الرحمن الرحيم ، إني أنا الله مالك يوم الدين ، إني أنا الله لم أزل ولا أزال ... إني أنا الله الواحد الصمد ... إني أنا الله الكبير المتعال . قال : ثم قال أبو عبد الله (﵇) من عنده ، والكبرياء رداءه فمن نازعه شيئا من ذلك أكبه الله في النار ، ثم قال : ما من عبد مؤمن يدعو بهن مقبلا قلبه إلى الله ﷿ إلا قضى حاجته "Ali ibn Ibrahim reported from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from one of his companions, that Abu Abd Allah said, "Allah has three hours in the night and three hours in the day when He praises Himself. He says, 'I am Allah, Lord of all worlds. I am Allah, the Most High, the Great. I am Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. I am Allah, the Forgiving, the Merciful. I am Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I am Allah, Master of the Day of Judgment. I am Allah. I have always existed, and I will always exist. I am Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge. I am Allah, the Great, the Most High.'"

Abu Abd Allah continued, "Greatness belongs to Allah, and majesty is His cloak. Allah will throw into the Fire anyone who disputes any part of that with Him. No believing servant calls upon Allah with these words while turning his heart toward Him except that Allah fulfills his need.""

The glorification of the hours strings the first person declaration by declaration, I, I am Allah, Lord of the worlds, I, I am Allah, the High, the Great. The doubled pronoun is the register of self-declaration, and Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ teaches it as the servant's supplication, with the promise that the need of whoever calls with it is granted.

Abu al-Hasan ﵇, al-Kafi, v2, p489 محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى ، عن أحمد بن محمد بن أبي نصر قال : قلت لأبي الحسن (﵇) : جعلت فداك إني قد سألت الله حاجة منذ كذا وكذا سنة وقد دخل قلبي من إبطائها شئ ، فقال : يا أحمد إياك والشيطان أن يكون له عليك سبيل حتى يقنطك ... فكن بالله أوثق فإنك على موعد من الله ، أليس الله ﷿ يقول : " وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع دعان (1) " وقال : " لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله (2) " وقال : " والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا (3) " فكن بالله ﷿ أوثق منك بغيره "Muhammad ibn Yahya reported from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said, "I said to Abu al-Hasan, 'May I be your ransom. I have asked Allah for something for many years, and its delay has troubled my heart.'"

Abu al-Hasan replied, "Ahmad, beware of Satan. Do not let him gain power over you and make you lose hope. Trust Allah more deeply. Allah has promised you. Does Allah not say, 'When My servants ask you about Me, I am near. I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me'? He also says, 'Do not lose hope in Allah's mercy.' He says, 'Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty.' Trust Allah more than you trust anyone else.""

The counselling hadith shows the school reading the I as address. A companion's hope was weakening after years of an unanswered request, and the Imam met him with the verse itself, asking whether Allah, exalted and majestic, has not said that He is near when His servants ask about Him. For the school the pronouns are a promise to stand on, and they have never been a puzzle to solve.

Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, relaying Ali ibn al-Husayn ﵇, al-Kafi, v1, p296 وبهذا الاسناد ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : كان علي بن الحسين صلوات الله عليه يقول : " إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر " صدق الله ﷿ أنزل الله القرآن في ليلة القدر " وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر " قال رسول الله ﵌ : لا أدري ، قال الله ﷿ " ليلة القدر خير من الف شهر " ليس فيها ليلة القدر ، قال لرسول الله ﵌ : وهل تدري لم هي خير من الف شهر ؟ قال لا ، قال : لأنها تنزل فيها الملائكة والروح بإذن ربهم من كل أمر ، وإذا أذن الله ﷿ بشئ فقد رضيه " سلام هي حتى مطلع الفجر " يقول : تسلم عليك يا محمد ملائكتي وروحي بسلامي من أول ما يهبطون إلى مطلع الفجر "Through the same chain, Abu Abd Allah reported that Ali ibn al-Husayn would say, "Allah spoke the truth when He said, 'We sent it down on the Night of Decree.' Allah sent down the Quran on the Night of Decree. 'What will make you know what the Night of Decree is?'"
The Messenger of Allah said, "I do not know."
Allah said, "The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months." No Night of Decree exists within those thousand months.
Allah asked the Messenger of Allah, "Do you know why it is better than a thousand months?"
The Messenger of Allah replied, "No."

Allah said, "The angels and the Spirit descend in it, by their Lord's permission, with every command. When Allah permits something, He is pleased with it. 'Peace it is until the rising of dawn.' My angels and My Spirit greet you, Muhammad, with My peace from the moment they descend until dawn rises.""

The Night of Decree narration layers the persons inside one report. Imam al-Sadiq ﵇ transmits the sequence from Ali ibn al-Husayn ﵇, the sura's We of the sending down, the third person of the angels' permission by their Lord's leave, and then Allah's own gloss in the first person, His angels and His spirit saluting Muhammad ﷺ with His peace. We, He, and My in five lines, one event, and no reporter felt a change of speaker.

Imam al-Kazim ﵇, al-Kafi, v1, p474 الحسين بن محمد ، عن معلى بن محمد ، عمن أخبره ، عن علي بن جعفر قال سمعت أبا الحسن ﵇ يقول : لما رأى رسول الله ﵌ تيما وعديا وبني أمية يركبون منبره أفظعه ، فأنزل الله ﵎ قرآنا يتأسى به : " وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى (5) " ثم أوحى إليه يا محمد إني أمرت فلم اطع فلا تجزع أنت إذا أمرت فلم تطع في وصيك "Husayn ibn Muhammad reported from Mulla ibn Muhammad, from someone who informed him, from Ali ibn Jafar, who said, "I heard Abu al-Hasan say, 'When the Messenger of Allah saw Taym, Adi, and Banu Umayyah climbing his pulpit, it distressed him. Allah sent down Quran to comfort him with, "When We said to the angels, 'Bow down before Adam,' they bowed down, except Iblis. He refused." Then Allah revealed to him, "Muhammad, I commanded and was disobeyed. Do not grieve when you command people regarding your successor and they disobey you."'""

And the consolation hadith joins the We-verse to the I-revelation directly. The Quran comforts the Prophet ﷺ with the We that spoke to the angels, and then Allah reveals to him in the first person that He commanded and was not obeyed. The We and the I are one Speaker at two registers, in the space of two sentences.

The riwa'i layer closes. The Ahl al-Bayt's ﵈ reports do not debate the pronouns. They pray with them, counsel with them, and narrate Allah answering in them. The Christian reader weighs these chains, the riwa'i or transmitted reports of the school, as testimony, and the grammar and usage they presuppose stand on ground he already accepts. What the rest of the tradition says is the last question, and it agrees.
7. The Sunni Mufassirun Say the Same

Source: al-Razi v28 p225; Abu Hayyan v7 p346; al-Alusi v12 p96; al-Sha'rawi v5 p232 Claim: the opponent's own tradition states the plural of majesty, explains it from the kings' usage, and calls the person-shifts eloquence Basis: Qur'an 51:47, 37:75
Al-Razi, a mufassir the polemic's own audience reveres, answered the polemic's own question eight centuries before it was asked.

al-Razi, Tafsir al-Razi, v28, p225 المسألة الرابعة : إذا كان المقصود إثبات التوحيد ، فكيف قال : ( بنيناها ) ولم يقل بنيتها أو بناها الله ؟ نقول قوله : ( بنينا ) أدل على عدم الشريك في التصرف والاستبداد وقوله بنيتها يمكن أن يكون فيه تشريك ... فإذن علم أن المراد جمع التعظيم وأفاد النص عظمته ، فالعظمة أنفى للشريك فثبت أن قوله : ( بنيناها ) أدل على نفي الشريك من بنيتها وبناها الله . فإن قيل : لم قلت : إن الجمع يدل على التعظيم ؟ قلنا الجواب من الوجهين . الأول : أن الكلام على قدر فهم السامع ، والسامع هو الإنسان ، والإنسان يقيس الشاهد على الغائب ، فإن الكبير عندهم من يفعل الشيء بجنده وخدمه ولا يباشر بنفسه ، فيقول الملك فعلنا أي فعله عبادنا بأمرنا ويكون في ذلك تعظيم ، فكذلك في حق الغائب "Fourth question. If the aim is to establish God's oneness, why does He say, "We built it," and not, "I built it," or, "God built it"? We answer, "We built it" more clearly shows that no one shares His control or independent power. "I built it" may suggest a partnership. The intended meaning is therefore the plural of majesty. The wording shows His greatness. His greatness excludes any partner. Thus, "We built it" more clearly denies a partner than "I built it" or "God built it."
If someone asks, "Why do you say that the plural shows majesty?" We answer in two ways.

First, speech follows what the listener can understand. The listener is human. People compare what they see with what they cannot see. They consider great a ruler who acts through his armies and servants without acting personally. A king says, "We did it," meaning, "Our servants did it by our command." This gives him majesty. The same applies to the Unseen."

Al-Razi asks it exactly. If the aim is oneness, why does the verse say We built, and not I built. His answer inverts the charge. The We is more decisive against a partner than the I, because majesty itself excludes a sharer, and his explanation of the register is the king's we. Among the Arabs the great one acts through his household and servants, so the king says we did, meaning that his servants did it at his command, and there is magnification in it. The polemic reads the We as plurality. The tradition's own systematizer read it as the tawhid-intensive form.

Abu Hayyan, al-Bahr al-Muhit, v7, p346 والمخصوص بالمدح محذوف تقديره : فلنعم المجيبون نحن ، وجاء بصيغة الجمع للعظمة والكبرياء لقوله : (فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ) "The one praised is omitted. Its meaning is, "How excellent are We in answering." He used the plural form to show majesty and greatness, as in His words, "We determined, and how excellent are We at determining.""

al-Alusi, Ruh al-Ma'ani, v12, p96 والجمع للعظمة والكبرياء وفيه من تعظيم أمر الإجابة ما فيه ؛ وأخرج ابن مردويه عن عائشة رضي اللّه تعالى عنها قالت : «كان النبي صلّى اللّه عليه وسلم إذا صلى في بيتي فمر بهذه الآية وَلَقَدْ نادانا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ قال : صدقت ربنا أنت أقرب من دعا وأقرب من بغى فنعم المدعو ونعم المعطي ونعم المسؤول ونعم المولى أنت ربنا ونعم النصير» "The plural expresses majesty and greatness, and it gives the act of answering great importance. Ibn Marduyah reported from Aisha that whenever the Prophet prayed in her home and passed this verse, "Noah called upon Us, and how excellent are We in answering," he said, "You have spoken the truth, our Lord. You are nearer than the one who calls upon You, and nearer than the one who transgresses. How excellent are You to call upon, how excellent are You to give, how excellent are You to ask, how excellent are You as Master. You are our Lord, and how excellent are You as Helper.""

Abu Hayyan on 37:75 states it in a clause, that the plural is for greatness and majesty. Al-Alusi adds the report of the Prophet's ﷺ prayer at the same verse, confessing the Lord's truth and His nearness to every caller. The plural-of-majesty verse and the second-person prayer stand together in one report, We on the page and You on the tongue, and no one in the chain found confusion.

al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, v5, p232 فالأسلوب القرآني حين يأتي ب «إني» يشير إلى وحدة الذات ، وحين يأتي ب «إنا» يشير إلى تجمع صفات الكمال ... لذلك لا بد من ضمير التعظيم الذي يقول فيه النحويون : إن «نحن» و «نا» للمعظم نفسه . وقد عظم الحق نفسه ؛ لأن الأمر هنا حشد صفات يتطلبها إيجاد الكون والقيام على أمر الكون . ... فسبحان رب فوق كل مظنة تعالى جلالا أن يحاط بذاته / إذا قال «إني» ذاك وحدة قدسه وإن قال «إنّا» ذاك حشد صفاته "When the Quranic style says, "I," it points to the oneness of the Divine Being. When it says, "We," it points to the gathering of perfect qualities. Therefore, the pronoun of majesty is necessary. Grammarians say that "We" and "Us" refer to the One who is great. The Truth has declared His own greatness because creating the universe and governing it require a gathering of attributes.

Glory be to a Lord beyond every assumption. His majesty is too high for His Being to be fully understood. When He says, "I," that expresses the oneness of His holiness. When He says, "We," that expresses the gathering of His attributes."

The modern tradition keeps the same reading. Al-Sha'rawi states the division of registers, the I for the oneness of the Essence, the We for the gathering of the attributes of perfection, and cites the grammarians' rule that the plural pronouns belong to the one magnifying himself. Whether one frames the We as majesty or as the attributes in act, the frame is register, and register does not count. And the register itself answers the Trinity's form of plurality. Attributes gathered in one essence are what the One has. Persons are who the One is. The Quran's We gathers the first and never divides the second.
The corroboration layer closes. Lexicon, usage, the book's own naming, the school's tafsir, the school's hadith, and the opponent's own commentators agree.
8. The Christian Canon on the Divine We

Holders cited: Augustine of Hippo, On the Trinity I.7.14; the Council of Nicaea, 325 Scripture: Genesis 1:26 and Deuteronomy 6:4, Westminster Leningrad Codex, Van Dyck Arabic, King James Version Claim: the Christian canon puts plural forms in God's mouth beside the strictest monotheism, and the church's reading of its own plural is creedal, not lexical
The method of the charge, reading a divine plural as plurality of agents, is the method Christians apply to Genesis.

Genesis 1:26, Westminster Leningrad Codex, King James Version וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ va-yomer elohim na'aseh adam be-tsalmenu ki-demutenu "And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness."

Deuteronomy 6:4, Westminster Leningrad Codex, King James Version שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ אֶחָֽד shema yisra'el YHWH elohenu YHWH echad "Hear, O Israel, the LORD our God is one LORD."

The same canon that says "let us make man in our image" also says that the LORD our God is one LORD, and says that the man has become as one of us (Genesis 3:22), bids us go down (Genesis 11:7), and asks who will go for us (Isaiah 6:8), where the I and the us share one sentence. Genesis 3:22 works like Maryam's we, set grammar implying a court around the speaker, and the heavenly-court reading carries it without a council of gods. Whichever reading is adopted, the Trinity's or the majesty's, must carry all of these verses alike. Augustine reads the Genesis plural as the Son's presence in creation, in On the Trinity I.7.14, arguing that were the Father alone to have made man without the Son, the plural of Genesis 1:26 would never have been written. The Council of Nicaea in 325 confessed one God the Father Almighty, maker of all things, and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom all things were made, God from God, of the same substance as the Father.

The comparison runs on four named tests. First, what each view asks a believer to accept about God. Second, whether each reading coheres with its own scripture. Third, which reading fits the words themselves. Fourth, which demands less of the text.

On the first test, each reading must square with its own scripture's monotheism, and both books hold the pair, plural forms and strict oneness, without dissolving either. On the second, the Quranic reading is a rule of the language the book speaks, settled by dictionaries, grammars, and usage, while the Trinitarian reading of Genesis reads the fourth-century creed back into Hebrew written a millennium before it. The synagogue's classic commentary reads the plural another way, as God consulting his heavenly court (Rashi on Genesis 1:26), and that reading is as old as the dispute.

On the third test, the words themselves. Augustine argues from the plural pronouns to plurality of persons, so the number of the pronoun is the load-bearing point, and the Hebrew grammar gives it no such freight. The noun of God stands under singular agreement, and Deuteronomy above shows a plural noun of God standing under one LORD, with nobody reading the morphology as a census. Genesis 1:26's verb is plural in form, like the Arabic nahnu, and that case is carried by the royal we of English, the queen's we are under one speaker, which is the point already made. On the fourth test, the plural of majesty needs no extra persons and no creed to import them, while the Trinitarian reading needs Nicaea to decide what the us means. The strongest form of the remaining objection deserves its name. Read the king's we as executors hidden inside the pronoun, and the divine We becomes Allah with his angels as his retinue. The note has already answered what that reading is worth. The book names the retinue wherever it acts, and the named retinue are creatures under command, worshippers who descend by permission and salute the Prophet ﷺ, which is not the plurality the charge wants. The charge needs helpers of the divine act who share the act's rank. The book gives creatures who carry out the act of the One. The grammar of majesty and the rule that names its co-agents together leave the retinue standing only as what has already been named, creatures under command, with nothing between creature and Creator inside the pronoun.

The agreement question has its own one-line answer. The English monarch says we are, and never we is, one speaker under plural agreement, and Latin grammarians gave the rule its name, pluralis majestatis. Plural agreement under a single will is the royal we's grammar in every language that has it, Arabic included, and the Hebrew noun of God under singular predicates shows the neighboring Semitic grammar carrying the same load.

The sophisticated form of the Christian reading does not rest on the pronoun at all. It reads Genesis through John's prologue, all things made through him, and through Paul's by him all things were created. That reading carries its agent into the Hebrew from outside it, and the four tests above measure exactly that move. The pronoun charge is the popular form of the case, and the creedal form rests on the creed. A method that convicts the Quran's We convicts Genesis first, and applied with one standard it convicts neither.

The Islamic case has stood throughout on the dictionaries, the poets, the book's own usage, the school's tafsir, the hadith of the Ahl al-Bayt ﵈, and the opponent's own commentators. The comparison shows the charge's method failing on its home ground. That is the difference between a reading drawn from the language and a reading required by the creed.
Final Verdict
The charge asked three questions, and the record answers each.

Does We mean others help Allah. No. Arabic has a plural of majesty, and the Kufan school's founding layer, al-Farra's, already reads it with the Quran's own verses as the textbook cases, in both directions, God saying We and Our of Himself and a creature addressing the one God in a plural. Abu Ali, two centuries on, states it as too famous in the language to need proof. The poets and kings used it, the Prophet ﷺ used it, the Imams ﵈ used it, and the Quran itself uses plural forms for single referents where no theology is at stake at all. Where helpers truly exist, the book names them, Allah and His angels, the angels and the Spirit by their Lord's permission, and keeps the We to itself. And the school's own reading of 5:55 rests on this grammar, so within the tradition the rule stands at the foundation.

When the Quran says He, who is speaking. Allah is speaking, presenting Himself in the third person the way the rhetoricians name and the Imams ﵈ practice, and the words travel a named relay. The Quran is Allah's speech placed on the tongue of a noble messenger, Jibril ﵇, carried to the Prophet's ﷺ heart, recited by the Prophet, taught to the servant. The say-verses make the relay visible, and the qudsi Fatiha makes all three persons audible in one report.

Why does the book move between We, He, and I. Because the registers do different work, and the language has a device for moving between them. The We carries majesty in creation and sending down. The He presents the Lord for the servant to learn of Him. The I answers where nearness and mercy are promised, and at Qur'an 2:186 the relay command is dropped so the Lord answers the questioner Himself. The shifts have a name, iltifat, a taxonomy, and stated purposes, and the sermon and prayer life of the Ahl al-Bayt ﵈ run on the same grammar.

The method that reads number into these pronouns would convict Genesis before it reaches the sura of the Reminder. Held to one standard, the We is majesty, the He is presence taught, and the I is the Lord answering, and the helpers the charge went looking for are exactly where the Quran put them, named, permitted, and creatures. And the burden runs the other way. The charge needs the plural to carry number, and every theologically neutral token in the book, the mosques, the callers, the single Prophet addressed in the plural, testifies that it does not.

A reader who abandons the pronoun and retreats to the creed, the Son through whom all things were made, has conceded the pronoun case. The Genesis likeness is the comparison the method itself draws when one grammar is held to both canons, and on that ground the dictionaries stand with the Quran. The creedal case begins at Nicaea, and it must be argued from there, on its own ground.

paragraphs: والثاني - انه جرى على تعظيم الذكر في خطاب الواحد بلفظ الجمع لعظم القدر كما يقول ذلك المتكلم ، قال الله تعالى " انا نحن نزلنا الذكر وانا له لحافظون " (1) وقال " ولقد خلقنا الانسان " (2) وما جرى مجراه . وروى النضر بن سمأل قال : سئل الخليل عن قوله " رب ارجعون " ففكر ثم قال : سألتموني عن شئ لا أحسنه ولا أعرف معناه ، والله أعلم ، لأنه جمع ، فاستحسن الناس منه ذلك

"“Send me back” has three explanations. First, it uses the plural to show greatness, as Allah says, “We sent down the Reminder,” and, “Have you not seen that Allah sent water down from the sky, then We brought forth?” Second, it means, “Angels of my Lord, send me back.” Third, the plural shows repeated pleading. It is as if he said, “Send me back, send me back.”"

"The second view is that this verse means Muhammad, since he is the one favored above all others. It says, “He raised some of them in ranks,” as a hint and an allusion. A person may do something great and be asked, “Who did this?” He may answer, “One of you,” or “Some of you,” while meaning himself. This sounds grander than naming himself directly. Al-Hutay'ah was asked who was the greatest poet. He named Zuhayr and al-Nabighah, then said, “If I wished, I could name the third.” He meant himself. Had he said, “If I wished, I could name myself,” the grandeur would have disappeared."

"His words, “Imru al-Qays shifted,” point to a fourth type, the change from speaking in the first person to addressing someone directly in “your night.” He mentioned these four because they are the most common and famous types. In the science of meanings, this shift differs from what the situation normally requires. In rhetoric, it expresses one meaning through different ways that make it clearer and more vivid. These two aspects give speech its own beauty and eloquence. In literary embellishment, it joins opposite forms within one meaning, so it is a type of meaningful embellishment. Thus, “your night” shifts from the first person to direct address."

"A plural word may mean one person. "The idolaters must not maintain Allah's mosques" means the Sacred Mosque. "Those who call out to you" refers to one man who called, "Muhammad, my praise is beauty and my insult is disgrace." "Let a group of believers witness their punishment" leaves the register of the single one and enters another. In the commentary it can be one, two, or more. "See what the messengers return with" refers to one person, as shown by the words, "Return to them." As for His words to Malik, "Cast both of you into Hell," reports from the People of the House say that Allah addressed the Prophet and the Commander of the Faithful. Al-Mubarrad said this is a dual verb used for emphasis, as if He said, "Cast, cast.""

The conclusion at the end says, "Flee to Allah," then, "Do not set up another god with Allah." This shows that these verses and proofs establish that Allah alone rules and governs."

n0093.caption: Tafsir al-Qummi, v2, p448
paragraphs: سورة الاخلاص مكية آياتها خمس ط (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قل هو الله أحد) اي هو الله الأحد وكان سبب نزولها ان اليهود جاءت إلى رسول الله ﵌ فقالت : ما نسب ربك ؟ فأنزل الله (قل هو الله أحد الله الصمد لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد) ومعنى قوله : أحد أحدي النعت كما قال رسول الله ﵌ : نور لا ظلام فيه وعلم لا جهل فيه وقوله : الصمد ، اي الذي لا مدخل فيه وقوله : لم يلد ، اي لم يحدث ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوا أحد ، قال : لا له كفو ولا شبيه ولا شريك ولا ظهير ولا معين .

"Surat al-Ikhlas was revealed in Mecca. It has five verses. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Say, 'He is Allah, the One.' The Jews came to the Messenger of Allah and asked, "What is your Lord's lineage?" Then Allah revealed, "Say, He is Allah, the One, Allah, the Everlasting Refuge. He did not beget, and He was not born. No one is equal to Him." Ahad means that His attributes are unique. The Messenger of Allah said, "He is a light free of darkness and knowledge free of ignorance." Al-Samad means the One with no opening within Him. "He did not beget" means that He did not bring anything into existence. "He was not born, and no one is equal to Him." He has no equal, no likeness, no partner, no supporter, and no helper."

n0100.caption: al-Mashhadi, Kanz al-Daqa'iq, v1, p118
paragraphs: وفي إيراد « إياك » دون « إياه » ، كما هو مقتضى الظاهر ، التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب . ومن النكتة الخاصة ، في الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ، في هذا المقام ، بعد اشتماله على فائدة عامة ، من جهة المتكلم ، وهي التصرف والافتنان في وجود الكلام واظهار القدرة عليها ، ومن جهة المخاطب ، وهي تطرية نشاطه في سماع الكلام ، وايقاظه للإصغاء إليه . أنه لما قيل : « إياك » بدل « إياه » ، فقد نزل الغائب بواسطة أوصافه المذكورة التي أوجب تميزه وانكشافه ، حتى صار كأنه تبدل خفاء غيبته ، بجلاء حضوره ، منزلة المخاطب في التمييز والظهور

"The use of iyyaka carries the speech from referring to someone absent into directly addressing Him. This shift has a general benefit. For the speaker, it shows skill and variety in expression. For the hearer, it renews attention and wakes the listener to hear carefully. Here it has a further purpose. The word iyyaka brings the One previously spoken of through His qualities into the position of one directly addressed. Those qualities distinguished Him and made Him known. The hiddenness of His absence became as clear as His presence. He therefore became like one directly addressed in clarity and distinction."

n0103.caption: al-Tabataba'i, al-Mizan, v3, p377
paragraphs: وأعلم أن في الآيات موارد من الالتفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب ومن خطاب الجمع إلى خطاب المفرد وبالعكس وفيها موارد من وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير كتكرر لفظ الجلالة في عدة مواضع والنكتة في الجميع ظاهرة للمتأمل

"Know that these verses include shifts from speaking about Allah to speaking directly to Him. They also shift between addressing many people and addressing one person. In some places, they use an explicit noun where a pronoun would usually appear, such as repeating the name Allah several times. A thoughtful reader can see the purpose of all these expressions."

n0105.caption: al-Mazandarani, Sharh Usul al-Kafi, v1, p122
paragraphs: (فقال : إذا قيل لهم) الضمير للناس في قوله تعالى : (يا أيها الناس كلوا مما في الأرض حلالاً طيباً ولا تتبعوا خطوات الشيطان) على سبيل الالتفات من الخطاب إلى الغيبة للتنبيه على بعدهم عن رتبة الخطاب بسبب سلوكهم طريق التقليد

"In the words, "When it is said to them," the pronoun refers to the people in Allah's words, "People, eat what is lawful and good on the earth. Do not follow Satan's footsteps." The speech shifts from directly addressing them to speaking about them. This alerts us that following imitation has kept them far from the rank of direct address."

n0106.caption: al-Mazandarani, Sharh Usul al-Kafi, v3, p204
paragraphs: (الذي لا يدركنا الغالي) الموصول صفة للنمط الأوسط وإفراده باعتبار اللّفظ والأصل أن يقول لا يدركه بالضمير للموصول إلاّ أنّه أتى بضمير المتكلّم من باب الالتفات من الغيبة إلى التكلّم للتصريح بالمقصود كما في قول أمير المؤمنين (﵇) : «أنا الّذي سمّتني أمي حيدرة»

"In “the extremist cannot grasp us,” the relative pronoun describes the middle pattern. It is singular because of its wording. The original wording would be “cannot grasp him,” using a pronoun that refers back to the relative pronoun. The verse brings the first-person pronoun, a shift from the third person to the first. It states the intended meaning plainly, as Amir al-Muminin said, “I am the one my mother named Haydara.”"

n0109.caption: al-Iskandari, al-Insaf, v2, p174
paragraphs: ثم التفات من التكلم إلى الغيبة بقوله - واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي الله وأن الله - وأصله واعلموا أنكم غير معجزي وأنى ، وفي هذا الالتفات بعد الالتفات الأول افتنان في أساليب البلاغة وتفخيم للشأن وتعظيم للأمر ... وكل هذا من حسنات الفصاحة

"Then the speech turns from "We" to speaking about Allah by name in, "Know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah..." Its original form was, "Know that you cannot escape Me, and that I..." This shift, after the first shift, shows variety in eloquent expression. It gives the matter greater weight and importance. All of this belongs to the beauties of eloquence."

n0113.caption: al-Tabrisi's gloss, in Bihar al-Anwar, v18, p173
paragraphs: وقال في قوله تعالى : " إنه لقول رسول كريم " أي إن القرآن قول رسول كريم على ربه وهو جبرئيل (﵇) ، وهو كلام الله أنزله على لسانه ، ثم وصف جبرئيل فقال : " ذي قوة " أي فيما كلف وامر به من العلم والعمل وتبليغ الرسالة ... " أمين " على وحي الله ورسالاته إلى أنبيائه

"Regarding Allah's words, "It is truly the word of a noble messenger," he said that the Quran is the word brought by a noble messenger before his Lord, who is Jibril. It is Allah's speech, which He sent down through Jibril. Allah then describes Jibril, "Possessing strength," meaning strength in the knowledge, actions, and delivery of the message entrusted to him. "Trustworthy," meaning trustworthy with Allah's revelation and His messages to His prophets."

n0117.caption: from al-Hasan, in Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v1, p118
paragraphs: روي عن الحسن أن سائلا سأل النبي ( ص ) أقريب ربنا فنناجيه أم بعيد فنناديه ؟ فنزلت الآية
"Hasan reported that a questioner asked the Prophet, "Is our Lord near, so we may speak quietly to Him, or far, so we must call out to Him?" Then the verse came down."

n0121.caption: Qur'an 2:186, Mukhtasar Majma' al-Bayan, v1, p118
paragraphs: وَإِذا سَأَلَكَ عِبادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذا دَعانِ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ
wa-idha sa'alaka 'ibadi 'anni fa-inni qarib. ujibu da'wata al-da'i idha da'an. fa-l-yastajibu li wa-l-yu'minu bi la'allahum yarshudun
"When My servants ask you about Me, I am near. I answer the call of the caller when he calls Me. Let them answer Me and believe in Me, so that they may be rightly guided."

n0123.caption: al-Saduq, 'Uyun Akhbar al-Rida ﵇, v1, p269
paragraphs: حدثنا محمد بن القاسم المفسر الأسترآبادي ﵁ قال : حدثنا يوسف بن محمد بن زياد وعلي بن محمد بن سيار عن أبويهما عن الحسن بن علي عن أبيه علي بن محمد عن أبيه محمد بن علي عن أبيه الرضا علي بن موسى عن أبيه موسى بن جعفر عن أبيه جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه محمد بن علي عن أبيه علي بن الحسين عن أبيه الحسين بن علي عن أبيه أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب ﵈ قال : قال رسول الله : قال الله ﷿ : قسمت فاتحه الكتاب بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سال إذا قال العبد (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم) قال الله جل جلاله : بدأ عبدي باسمي وحق على أن أتمم له أموره وأبارك له في أحواله فإذا قال : (الحمد لله رب العالمين) قال الله ﷿ : حمدني عبدي وعلم أن النعم التي له من عندي وان البلايا التي دفعت عنه فبطولي أشهدكم انى أضيف له إلى نعم الدنيا نعم الآخرة ... فإذا قال : (إياك نعبد) قال الله ﷿ : صدق عبدي إياي يعبد ... فإذا قال : (اهدنا الصراط المستقيم) إلى آخر السورة قال الله ﷿ : هذا لعبدي ولعبدي ما سال

"Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, the commentator from Astarabad, reported from Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, from their fathers, from Hasan ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father al-Rida Ali ibn Musa, from his father Musa ibn Jafar, from his father Jafar ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Amir al-Muminin Ali ibn Abi Talib. The Messenger of Allah said that Allah said, "I divided the Opening of the Book between Me and My servant. Half belongs to Me, and half belongs to My servant. My servant will receive what he asks for."

n0129.caption: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, al-Kafi, v2, p515
paragraphs: علي بن إبراهيم ، عن أبيه ، عن صفوان بن يحيى ، عن إسحاق بن عمار ، عن بعض أصحابه ، عن أبي عبد الله (﵇) قال : إن لله ﷿ ثلاث ساعات في الليل وثلاث ساعات في النهار يمجد فيهن نفسه ... يقول : إني أنا الله رب العالمين ، إني أنا الله العلي العظيم ، إني أنا الله العزيز الحكيم ، إني أنا الله الغفور الرحيم ، إني أنا الله الرحمن الرحيم ، إني أنا الله مالك يوم الدين ، إني أنا الله لم أزل ولا أزال ... إني أنا الله الواحد الصمد ... إني أنا الله الكبير المتعال . قال : ثم قال أبو عبد الله (﵇) من عنده ، والكبرياء رداءه فمن نازعه شيئا من ذلك أكبه الله في النار ، ثم قال : ما من عبد مؤمن يدعو بهن مقبلا قلبه إلى الله ﷿ إلا قضى حاجته

"Ali ibn Ibrahim reported from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from one of his companions, that Abu Abd Allah said, "Allah has three hours in the night and three hours in the day when He praises Himself. He says, 'I am Allah, Lord of all worlds. I am Allah, the Most High, the Great. I am Allah, the Mighty, the Wise. I am Allah, the Forgiving, the Merciful. I am Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I am Allah, Master of the Day of Judgment. I am Allah. I have always existed, and I will always exist. I am Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge. I am Allah, the Great, the Most High.'"

n0132.caption: Abu al-Hasan ﵇, al-Kafi, v2, p489
paragraphs: محمد بن يحيى ، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى ، عن أحمد بن محمد بن أبي نصر قال : قلت لأبي الحسن (﵇) : جعلت فداك إني قد سألت الله حاجة منذ كذا وكذا سنة وقد دخل قلبي من إبطائها شئ ، فقال : يا أحمد إياك والشيطان أن يكون له عليك سبيل حتى يقنطك ... فكن بالله أوثق فإنك على موعد من الله ، أليس الله ﷿ يقول : " وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع دعان (1) " وقال : " لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله (2) " وقال : " والله يعدكم مغفرة منه وفضلا (3) " فكن بالله ﷿ أوثق منك بغيره

"Muhammad ibn Yahya reported from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said, "I said to Abu al-Hasan, 'May I be your ransom. I have asked Allah for something for many years, and its delay has troubled my heart.'"

n0135.caption: Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, relaying Ali ibn al-Husayn ﵇, al-Kafi, v1, p296
paragraphs: وبهذا الاسناد ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : كان علي بن الحسين صلوات الله عليه يقول : " إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر " صدق الله ﷿ أنزل الله القرآن في ليلة القدر " وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر " قال رسول الله ﵌ : لا أدري ، قال الله ﷿ " ليلة القدر خير من الف شهر " ليس فيها ليلة القدر ، قال لرسول الله ﵌ : وهل تدري لم هي خير من الف شهر ؟ قال لا ، قال : لأنها تنزل فيها الملائكة والروح بإذن ربهم من كل أمر ، وإذا أذن الله ﷿ بشئ فقد رضيه " سلام هي حتى مطلع الفجر " يقول : تسلم عليك يا محمد ملائكتي وروحي بسلامي من أول ما يهبطون إلى مطلع الفجر

"Through the same chain, Abu Abd Allah reported that Ali ibn al-Husayn would say, "Allah spoke the truth when He said, 'We sent it down on the Night of Decree.' Allah sent down the Quran on the Night of Decree. 'What will make you know what the Night of Decree is?'"

n0142.caption: Imam al-Kazim ﵇, al-Kafi, v1, p474
paragraphs: الحسين بن محمد ، عن معلى بن محمد ، عمن أخبره ، عن علي بن جعفر قال سمعت أبا الحسن ﵇ يقول : لما رأى رسول الله ﵌ تيما وعديا وبني أمية يركبون منبره أفظعه ، فأنزل الله ﵎ قرآنا يتأسى به : " وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا لآدم فسجدوا إلا إبليس أبى (5) " ثم أوحى إليه يا محمد إني أمرت فلم اطع فلا تجزع أنت إذا أمرت فلم تطع في وصيك

"Husayn ibn Muhammad reported from Mulla ibn Muhammad, from someone who informed him, from Ali ibn Jafar, who said, "I heard Abu al-Hasan say, 'When the Messenger of Allah saw Taym, Adi, and Banu Umayyah climbing his pulpit, it distressed him. Allah sent down Quran to comfort him with, "When We said to the angels, 'Bow down before Adam,' they bowed down, except Iblis. He refused." Then Allah revealed to him, "Muhammad, I commanded and was disobeyed. Do not grieve when you command people regarding your successor and they disobey you."'""

n0148.caption: al-Razi, Tafsir al-Razi, v28, p225
paragraphs: المسألة الرابعة : إذا كان المقصود إثبات التوحيد ، فكيف قال : ( بنيناها ) ولم يقل بنيتها أو بناها الله ؟ نقول قوله : ( بنينا ) أدل على عدم الشريك في التصرف والاستبداد وقوله بنيتها يمكن أن يكون فيه تشريك ... فإذن علم أن المراد جمع التعظيم وأفاد النص عظمته ، فالعظمة أنفى للشريك فثبت أن قوله : ( بنيناها ) أدل على نفي الشريك من بنيتها وبناها الله . فإن قيل : لم قلت : إن الجمع يدل على التعظيم ؟ قلنا الجواب من الوجهين . الأول : أن الكلام على قدر فهم السامع ، والسامع هو الإنسان ، والإنسان يقيس الشاهد على الغائب ، فإن الكبير عندهم من يفعل الشيء بجنده وخدمه ولا يباشر بنفسه ، فيقول الملك فعلنا أي فعله عبادنا بأمرنا ويكون في ذلك تعظيم ، فكذلك في حق الغائب

"Fourth question. If the aim is to establish God's oneness, why does He say, "We built it," and not, "I built it," or, "God built it"? We answer, "We built it" more clearly shows that no one shares His control or independent power. "I built it" may suggest a partnership. The intended meaning is therefore the plural of majesty. The wording shows His greatness. His greatness excludes any partner. Thus, "We built it" more clearly denies a partner than "I built it" or "God built it."

n0152.caption: Abu Hayyan, al-Bahr al-Muhit, v7, p346
paragraphs: والمخصوص بالمدح محذوف تقديره : فلنعم المجيبون نحن ، وجاء بصيغة الجمع للعظمة والكبرياء لقوله : (فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ)

"The one praised is omitted. Its meaning is, "How excellent are We in answering." He used the plural form to show majesty and greatness, as in His words, "We determined, and how excellent are We at determining.""

n0153.caption: al-Alusi, Ruh al-Ma'ani, v12, p96
paragraphs: والجمع للعظمة والكبرياء وفيه من تعظيم أمر الإجابة ما فيه ؛ وأخرج ابن مردويه عن عائشة رضي اللّه تعالى عنها قالت : «كان النبي صلّى اللّه عليه وسلم إذا صلى في بيتي فمر بهذه الآية وَلَقَدْ نادانا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ قال : صدقت ربنا أنت أقرب من دعا وأقرب من بغى فنعم المدعو ونعم المعطي ونعم المسؤول ونعم المولى أنت ربنا ونعم النصير»

"The plural expresses majesty and greatness, and it gives the act of answering great importance. Ibn Marduyah reported from Aisha that whenever the Prophet prayed in her home and passed this verse, "Noah called upon Us, and how excellent are We in answering," he said, "You have spoken the truth, our Lord. You are nearer than the one who calls upon You, and nearer than the one who transgresses. How excellent are You to call upon, how excellent are You to give, how excellent are You to ask, how excellent are You as Master. You are our Lord, and how excellent are You as Helper.""

n0155.caption: al-Sha'rawi, Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, v5, p232
paragraphs: فالأسلوب القرآني حين يأتي ب «إني» يشير إلى وحدة الذات ، وحين يأتي ب «إنا» يشير إلى تجمع صفات الكمال ... لذلك لا بد من ضمير التعظيم الذي يقول فيه النحويون : إن «نحن» و «نا» للمعظم نفسه . وقد عظم الحق نفسه ؛ لأن الأمر هنا حشد صفات يتطلبها إيجاد الكون والقيام على أمر الكون . ... فسبحان رب فوق كل مظنة تعالى جلالا أن يحاط بذاته / إذا قال «إني» ذاك وحدة قدسه وإن قال «إنّا» ذاك حشد صفاته

"When the Quranic style says, "I," it points to the oneness of the Divine Being. When it says, "We," it points to the gathering of perfect qualities. Therefore, the pronoun of majesty is necessary. Grammarians say that "We" and "Us" refer to the One who is great. The Truth has declared His own greatness because creating the universe and governing it require a gathering of attributes.

n0162.caption: Genesis 1:26, Westminster Leningrad Codex, King James Version
paragraphs: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים נַֽעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֛ם בְּצַלְמֵ֖נוּ כִּדְמוּתֵ֑נוּ
va-yomer elohim na'aseh adam be-tsalmenu ki-demutenu
"And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness."

n0163.caption: Deuteronomy 6:4, Westminster Leningrad Codex, King James Version
paragraphs: שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ אֶחָֽד
shema yisra'el YHWH elohenu YHWH echad
"Hear, O Israel, the LORD our God is one LORD."
